ENISA is the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, which supports cybersecurity policy, guidance, and coordination across Europe.

entra-id
Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft’s cloud identity service, formerly called Azure Active Directory.
entry point concept
An entry point is the place or method an attacker, program, or process first uses to get into a system or workflow.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.
Errol Weiss other
Errol Weiss is a named person quoted in the article.
Escalate privileges technique
To escalate privileges means to gain higher-level access on a system than you were originally allowed to have.
Escalation concept
An escalation is a security case passed to a person or higher-level team because it needs additional attention or action.
Essential Services concept
Services people depend on for daily life and public safety, such as power, water, healthcare, and government services.
europe
Europe is a continent often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regulations, victims, threat activity, or law enforcement.
European Commission organization
European Commission is the European Union's executive body that proposes laws, enforces rules, and oversees policy.
European Union's Cyber Resilience Act concept
The European Union's Cyber Resilience Act is an EU law that sets cybersecurity requirements for certain products with digital elements.
european-union
The European Union is a political and economic union of European countries that also creates cybersecurity and privacy rules.

Collecting and reviewing system records to understand actions, changes, and possible security issues.
event logs concept
Event logs are records created by computers and applications that show important actions, errors, and security activity.

EvilTokens tool

excessive access concept
Excessive access means a person or account has more permissions than they actually need, increasing security risk.
excessive permissions vulnerability

Excessive privileges mean an account or program has more access rights than it actually needs.

Exchange Online product
Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service in Microsoft 365.
exchange-server-2019 product
exchange-server-2019 refers to Microsoft Exchange Server 2019, an on-premises email and calendar server product.

Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.

also: ETD
exploit technique
An exploit is code or a method that takes advantage of a security flaw to make something happen that should not be allowed.
exploit kit tool
An exploit kit is a package of tools criminals use to automatically find and exploit vulnerable browsers, plugins, or systems.
Exploitability concept
Exploitability describes how easily an attacker can take advantage of a security weakness.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
Exploited technique
Exploited means attackers successfully took advantage of a weakness in software or a system.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.

Exploits are code or techniques that take advantage of software vulnerabilities.
Exposed concept
Accessible in a way that could allow a threat to reach or affect a system.
exposed credentials concept
Login details that have been accidentally published or stolen, granting unauthorized access.

fallback concept

federal intelligence authorities organization
National government agencies that collect, analyze, or share intelligence about threats.

also: FSB
fetch tool

Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform.
Microsoft Defender product
Microsoft Defender is Microsoft’s built-in security software for detecting and blocking malware and other threats.
Microsoft Defender XDR product
Microsoft Defender XDR is Microsoft's extended detection and response platform for finding and responding to threats across systems.
also: Defender XDR
Microsoft Entra ID product
Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud identity service for managing users, logins, apps, and access permissions.
Microsoft Sentinel product
Microsoft Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-based security information and event management and response platform.
microsoft-365
Microsoft 365 is Microsoft’s cloud productivity and security suite including Office apps, email, storage, and collaboration tools.
microsoft-graph product
microsoft-graph refers to Microsoft's Graph API, which lets software access Microsoft cloud data and identity information.
Midnight Blizzard threat-actor
Midnight Blizzard is a Russia-linked threat actor group known for cyber-espionage activity.
minimum release age concept
Minimum release age is a safety rule that blocks brand-new package versions until they have existed for a set amount of time.
Mirroring cosigner technique
A mirroring cosigner independently copies and checks a certificate log, then adds its signature to improve trust in that log.
Misaligned product
An AI-generated film project referenced in reporting.
misuse concept
Misuse is using a system, account, or feature in a harmful or unauthorized way.
mitiga
Mitiga is a cloud incident response and threat detection company.
mitigate concept
To mitigate a security problem means to reduce its impact or make it harder to exploit, even if it is not fully eliminated.
mitigation concept
A measure that reduces the likelihood or impact of a security problem.
mitigations concept
Mitigations are steps taken to reduce the chance or impact of a security problem.
ML-DSA protocol
ML-DSA is a post-quantum digital signature algorithm selected for standardized use.
ML-KEM protocol
ML-KEM is a post-quantum algorithm used for establishing shared cryptographic keys securely.
ML-KEM-768 protocol
ML-KEM-768 is a NIST-standardized post-quantum key encapsulation method used to help two systems establish a shared encryption key.
mobile device management system tool
A mobile device management system is software an organization uses to configure, monitor, and secure phones, tablets, or laptops.
model context protocol (MCP) protocol
Model Context Protocol is a standard that helps AI applications connect to external tools, data sources, and services in a consistent way.
also: MCP
Model Context Protocol Python SDK tool
The Model Context Protocol Python SDK is an official Python library for building software that uses the Model Context Protocol.
money laundering concept
The illegal process of making money obtained from crime appear to come from a legitimate source.
money mules concept
Money mules are people who move stolen or illegal money for criminals, sometimes without realizing it.
monitoring systems tool
Monitoring systems are tools that watch networks, computers, applications, or services for problems and suspicious activity.
monorepo concept
A monorepo is a single code repository that holds multiple projects or components together.
Monorepos concept
Monorepos are single code repositories that hold multiple projects or services together.
Monthly ETD Report product
A Monthly ETD Report is a recurring security report that summarizes threat-hunting findings, observations, and risks.
also: technical document
Monthly Windows Updates product
Microsoft's regular monthly releases of security fixes, bug fixes, and Windows improvements.
Mozilla organization
Mozilla is the organization behind the Firefox web browser and other open internet projects.
Mozilla Firefox product
Mozilla Firefox is a popular web browser made by Mozilla.
mprotect tool
mprotect is a computer-system function that changes which programs are allowed to read, write, or run code in a memory area.
MSI tool
MSI usually refers to Microsoft Installer packages used to install software on Windows.
MSI installers concept
MSI installers are Windows installation packages used to install, update, or remove software.
multi-factor authentication concept
Multi-factor authentication is a login method that asks users to prove who they are in more than one way.
also: strong authentication, a second login step, second factor
MySQL product
MySQL is a database system used to store and retrieve structured information.
Namespace concept
A namespace is a named container used to keep identifiers, resources, or settings separate from others so they do not conflict.
National Cyber Security Center organization
National Cyber Security Center is the name used by government cyber security agencies that provide national cyber defense guidance and response.
National Cyber Security Centre organization
The National Cyber Security Centre is the UK government organization that gives cybersecurity guidance and helps respond to major cyber incidents.
Native audit technique
Native audit means using a system’s built-in logging or auditing features to record activity and investigate what happened.
NDcPP concept
NDcPP is a Common Criteria security standard and protection profile used to evaluate network devices.
Negotiate protocol
Negotiate is a Windows authentication scheme that automatically chooses a method such as Kerberos or NTLM for logging in securely.
netherlands
The Netherlands is a European country often mentioned in cybersecurity stories involving hosting, law enforcement, or victims.
NetScaler product
NetScaler is a Citrix networking product line used for application delivery, load balancing, and secure remote access.
NetScaler ADC product
NetScaler ADC is an application delivery controller product used to manage, optimize, and secure traffic to web applications.
NetScaler Gateway product
NetScaler Gateway is a remote access and application access product used to let users securely connect to internal applications.
network controls concept
Network controls are security settings or tools that manage what traffic can enter, leave, or move within a network.
Network Level concept
Network level refers to controls, decisions, or analysis applied to traffic, connections, or infrastructure rather than individual users or apps.
Network Monitoring concept
Network monitoring is watching network traffic and devices to spot outages, unusual behavior, or attacks.
Network segmentation technique
Network segmentation is splitting a network into separate sections so a problem or attacker in one area cannot easily reach everything else.
New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research organization
An Australian government agency that collects and analyzes crime statistics in New South Wales.
Next.js product
Next.js is a popular web-development framework used to build websites and web applications with React.
Nimbus product
Nimbus is Cloudflare's family of public certificate-transparency logs.
NIS2 concept
NIS2 is a European Union cybersecurity directive that sets security and reporting requirements for important organizations.
NIST organization
NIST is the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which creates widely used security standards and guidance.
Nitro product
A software project in the JavaScript ecosystem used for building web servers and applications.
No-code concept
No-code describes software designed to let people create workflows or applications without writing programming code.
Node product
Node usually refers to Node.js, a runtime that lets JavaScript run outside a web browser.
also: node root
Node.js product
Node.js is a JavaScript runtime used to build server-side and command-line applications.
Node.js product
Node.js is a platform that lets developers run JavaScript code outside a web browser, often on servers.
node_modules concept
node_modules is the folder where Node.js projects usually store downloaded third-party packages and dependencies.
non-human identities concept
Non-human identities are digital identities used by systems, services, or automated processes instead of people.
North America other
North America is a geographic region including countries such as the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
npm product
npm is the main package manager and public registry for JavaScript software libraries.
npm package concept
An npm package is a reusable JavaScript software bundle that developers can install from the npm ecosystem.
npm registry product
The npm registry is the main online repository where JavaScript packages are published and downloaded.
nsppe tool
nsppe is a named NetScaler-related process, component, or tool referenced in security reporting.
Nub tool
A software package-management tool referenced in security reporting.
Nuxt product
Nuxt is a web application framework built on Vue.js for creating websites and server-rendered applications.
NVIDIA organization
NVIDIA is a technology company known for graphics chips, AI hardware, and related software.
OAuth protocol
An authorization protocol that allows a user to grant a third-party application limited access to their resources without sharing their password.
OAuth application protocol
An application that uses OAuth permissions to access an account without receiving the user’s password.
OAuth applications protocol
OAuth applications are apps that use OAuth permissions to access accounts or data without directly sharing passwords.
OAuth client registrations concept
OAuth client registrations are records that identify an application to an authorization service and define what access it may request.
OAuth client secrets concept
OAuth client secrets are private values an app uses to prove its identity to an OAuth service.
OAuth credentials protocol
OAuth credentials are access details used to authorize one service to connect to another.
OAuth token protocol
An OAuth token is a digital credential that lets an app access a user’s account or data without knowing the user’s password.
OAuthClientProvider tool
A software component that helps an application use OAuth to obtain access credentials from a login service.
obfuscated technique
Obfuscated means code or text has been deliberately made hard to read so people or security tools cannot easily understand what it does.
objective concept
An objective is the goal an attacker or security operation is trying to achieve.
Odido organization
Odido is a Dutch telecommunications company that provides mobile and internet services.
offboarding concept
Offboarding is the process of removing a departing worker's accounts, access, and equipment.
Office 365 product
Office 365 is Microsoft’s cloud-based email, office apps, and collaboration service, now commonly called Microsoft 365.
Office 365 Exchange Online product
Microsoft's cloud-based service for business email, calendars, and mailboxes.
Okta organization
Okta is a company that provides identity and login management services for organizations.
Okta Audit Logs tool
Records created by Okta that show sign-in events, administrative changes, and other activity in an identity system.
Okta FastPass product
An Okta sign-in feature that lets users authenticate with a device-based prompt instead of typing a password.
on-device concept
On-device means processing happens locally on a user’s phone, computer, or other device instead of on a remote server.
on-premises concept
On-premises means software or hardware runs in an organization’s own facilities instead of in the cloud.
One-time code concept
A one-time code is a short temporary code used to confirm identity during login or a transaction.
also: one-time code sent by email
online services concept
Online services are websites, apps, or internet-based systems that provide functions to users over the internet.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.
Open-Source Codebases concept
Collections of software source code that are publicly available for people to inspect, use, and modify.
open-source intelligence technique
Open-source intelligence is information gathered from public sources such as websites, social media, records, and news reports.
also: open-source intelligence (OSINT) review
Open-source projects concept
Open-source projects are software projects whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, or contribute to.
Open-source reporting concept
Open-source reporting is information gathered from publicly available sources rather than private intelligence or classified channels.
open-source threat intelligence concept
Open-source threat intelligence is security information about threats that comes from publicly available sources.
openai organization
OpenAI is an AI company known for ChatGPT and GPT language models.
also: The ChatGPT maker, the company, AI company, frontier AI lab
OpenAI Agent product
An AI-based software agent made by OpenAI that can carry out tasks such as searching for information or using online services.
OpenAI Codex product
OpenAI Codex is an AI coding system designed to understand and generate computer code from natural-language instructions.
also: public "openai/codex" repository
OpenAPI v3 protocol
OpenAPI v3 is a standard format for describing how an application programming interface accepts requests and returns responses.
Operating system concept
An operating system is the main software that manages a computer or phone, such as Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS.
Operator tool
An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
Operator Lifecycle Manager tool
Operator Lifecycle Manager is a Kubernetes tool for installing, updating, and managing Kubernetes operators.
OperatorHub organization
OperatorHub is an online catalog for finding and installing Kubernetes operators.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
OperTraitor tool
OperTraitor is an open-source tool that analyzes Kubernetes operator permissions and identifies potentially excessive access.
oracle
Oracle is a technology company known for databases, enterprise software, cloud services, and Java-related products.
Oracle PeopleSoft product
Oracle PeopleSoft is a suite of enterprise applications used for business functions such as HR, finance, and administration.
Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability
An Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day is a previously unknown security flaw in Oracle PeopleSoft that attackers may exploit before a fix is available.
Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day flaw vulnerability
An Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day flaw is a previously unknown vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft software that attackers may exploit before a patch is available.
ORB tool
ORB, short for Operational Relay Box, refers to intermediary internet infrastructure that threat actors use to hide or route their activity.
order data concept
Order data is information about purchases, such as customer details, items bought, prices, and shipping information.
order details concept
Order details are information about a customer's purchase, such as products, prices, delivery, and payment-related records.
order history concept
Order history is the record of past purchases or transactions tied to a customer account.
OriginTLSKeyExchangeGroup other
OriginTLSKeyExchangeGroup is a log field that records the cryptographic key-exchange algorithm used between Cloudflare and an origin server.
OSINT concept
OSINT, or open-source intelligence, is information gathered from publicly available sources such as websites, social media, and records.
out-of-bounds write vulnerability
A memory corruption vulnerability where a program writes data outside the allocated memory buffer, often leading to code execution.
Out-of-bounds write flaw vulnerability
An out-of-bounds write flaw is a memory bug where software writes data outside the area it was supposed to use.
out-of-bounds write weakness vulnerability
An out-of-bounds write weakness is a bug where software writes data past the allowed memory area, which can crash programs or let attackers run code.
outbound concept
Outbound traffic is network communication that leaves a device or organization and goes to an outside destination.
Outdated concept
Outdated means software, data, or settings are old and may be missing important fixes or protections.
Own Domain Spoofing technique
Own Domain Spoofing is an email deception technique in which an attacker forges an address to look like it came from the recipient's own organization.
OX Security organization
A cybersecurity company providing software supply chain security and posture management solutions.
package manager tool
A package manager is software that installs, updates, and manages libraries or applications for developers and operating systems.
package release concept
A package release is a published version of a software library or component that others can download and use.
package versions concept
Package versions are numbered releases of software components that help track updates and fixes.
package-lock.json product
An npm lockfile that records the exact versions of packages installed for a project.
Packet concept
A packet is a small chunk of data sent across a network.
Packets concept
Packets are small chunks of data sent across a network.
Palo Alto Networks organization
A leading global cybersecurity company known for next-generation firewalls and advanced cloud security.
PAM concept
Privileged Access Management, a set of tools and policies to secure, control, and monitor access to critical systems and data.
Panoramic Awareness product
A Mitiga security capability that combines evidence from cloud, software-as-a-service, and identity systems into a unified view of activity.
Password hash concept
A password hash is a scrambled mathematical representation of a password that a service stores instead of the password itself.
password hashes concept
Password hashes are scrambled versions of passwords that systems store so they do not have to keep the plain passwords.
password reset concept
The process of changing a user's password, typically after they've forgotten it or it's been compromised.
password resets concept
The process of changing or recovering a password, often used when a user forgets their current password.
password-protected archive concept
A password-protected archive is a compressed file, such as a ZIP, that requires a password to open and is sometimes used to hide malicious files from scanners.
password-spraying technique
Password spraying is when attackers try a few common passwords across many accounts to avoid quick lockouts.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
Patient Records concept
Documents and data containing an individual's medical history, treatment, and healthcare information.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
Payment card information concept
Payment card information is data from credit or debit cards, such as card numbers, names, expiration dates, or security codes.
Payment data concept
Payment data is information used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or transaction records.
payment information concept
Payment information is data used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or payment account identifiers.
PDF product
PDF is a common document file format used to preserve how text and images appear across devices.
PeopleSoft product
PeopleSoft is Oracle enterprise software used for business functions such as human resources, finance, and administration.
Periodic Access Reviews technique
Regular checks that confirm users still have the permissions they need and no more.
Permission enumeration technique
A technique in which an attacker checks what users, accounts, roles, or services are allowed to access.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personal details concept
Personal details are information about a person, such as their name, address, phone number, or financial data, that can be misused if stolen.
Personal Devices concept
Phones, computers, or tablets owned by an individual rather than managed by an employer.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
personally identifiable information concept
Personally identifiable information is data that can identify a person, such as a name, address, Social Security number, or email address.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
also: password phishing
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing emails technique
Phishing emails are fake messages designed to trick people into revealing information or clicking harmful links.
phishing kit tool
A pre-packaged set of tools and templates that allows even non-technical criminals to launch phishing campaigns easily.
phishing-resistant MFA concept
Phishing-resistant MFA is multi-factor authentication designed so fake login pages cannot easily steal or reuse the login proof.
phishing-resistant sign-in technique
Phishing-resistant sign-in uses login methods, such as hardware security keys or passkeys, that are hard for fake websites to trick.
phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
PHP web shell malware
A PHP web shell is a malicious script uploaded to a web server that lets an attacker run commands through a browser.
PHP web shells tool
PHP web shells are small scripts attackers place on a web server so they can run commands through a browser.
pig-butchering technique
Pig-butchering is a long-running scam where criminals build trust with a victim before tricking them into fake investments.
PII concept
PII means personally identifiable information, such as names, addresses, ID numbers, or other data that can identify a person.
PINs concept
PINs are short secret number codes used to verify identity or authorize access.
pivot technique
A pivot is an investigative move where one clue is used to find another related clue, such as moving from a domain to linked IP addresses.
PKCE protocol
PKCE is an OAuth security feature that helps stop attackers from stealing login authorization codes.
PKCE proof key protocol
A PKCE proof key is a secret value used during OAuth sign-in to help prevent a stolen authorization code from being reused.
plaintext concept
Plaintext is information stored or sent in a readable, unprotected form.
pnpm tool
pnpm is a fast JavaScript package manager used to install and manage project dependencies.
also: pnpm 12
pnpm-lock.yaml product
A lockfile that records the exact software package versions used by a pnpm project.
pod concept
A pod is the basic Kubernetes unit that runs one or more related containers together.
also: pods
Post-compromise activity technique
Post-compromise activity is what attackers do after they have already broken into a system.
post-exploitation activity technique
Post-exploitation activity is what an attacker does after first breaking into a system, such as exploring, stealing data, or expanding access.
post-quantum concept
Post-quantum describes cryptography designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers.
also: post-quantum Internet, post-quantum threat, post-quantum world
post-quantum authentication concept
Post-quantum authentication means proving identity using methods designed to remain secure even against future quantum computers.
post-quantum cryptography concept
Post-quantum cryptography is encryption and digital signature technology designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers.
post-quantum encryption concept
Post-quantum encryption is encryption designed to stay secure even if attackers have powerful future quantum computers.
post-quantum signatures concept
Post-quantum signatures are digital signatures designed to remain secure even against future quantum computers.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
PowerShell commands tool
PowerShell commands are instructions run in Microsoft's powerful Windows automation shell, often used by administrators and attackers alike.
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
Precise concept
Carefully targeted and intended to avoid unnecessary effects.
Privacy Policy concept
A Privacy Policy explains how a company or service collects, uses, stores, and shares people's personal information.
Private information concept
Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
private messages concept
Private messages are direct messages meant to be visible only to selected users.
PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider tool
A software component that uses a private-key-signed JSON Web Token to authenticate an OAuth client.
Privileged Access Management concept
Privileged Access Management is the practice of controlling and monitoring powerful administrator accounts.
privileged account concept
A privileged account is a user account with extra powers, such as changing settings, reading sensitive data, or managing other users.
Privileged accounts concept
Privileged accounts are user or service accounts with powerful permissions that can make major changes to systems or data.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
proactive threat hunting technique
Proactive threat hunting is actively searching for signs of attackers before an alert or confirmed incident appears.
also: proactive service, proactive hunting
processor concept
A processor is the main chip in a computer that runs instructions and performs calculations.
production environment concept
A production environment is the live system that real users or customers depend on, unlike a test environment.
Production environments concept
Production environments are the live systems that real users depend on, as opposed to test or development systems.
Production infrastructure concept
Production infrastructure is the real servers, cloud services, and systems that run live applications for users.
production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
Prometurbo product
Prometurbo is an IBM Turbonomic component for Kubernetes that helps manage resource allocation.
Prometurbo operator tool
The Prometurbo operator is a Kubernetes operator associated with IBM Turbonomic.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
also: a prompt injection, malicious prompt
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
proof-of-concept exploits tool
Proof-of-concept exploits are example programs or instructions that show a security flaw can be used in practice.
Protective Layer concept
An additional security control added to help block or limit attacks.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
public certificate authority organization
A public certificate authority is an organization trusted by browsers to issue certificates that secure public websites.
also: public CA, CA
public data concept
Public data is information that is openly available or accessible without special permission.
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
public IP address concept
A public IP address is an internet-reachable network address that can be accessed from outside a private network.
public repository concept
A public repository is an online code or file storage area that anyone can view and sometimes copy from.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
Publicly disclosed concept
Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
push technique
A push is the act of sending local code changes to a remote source-code repository such as GitHub.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
Quantum threat-actor
A ransomware threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
quantum computers concept
Quantum computers are computers that use quantum physics and may someday solve some problems much faster than normal computers.
Quantum-resistant Root Program product
The Quantum-resistant Root Program is Chrome's program for evaluating post-quantum certificate roots and authorities.
Queries concept
Requests sent to a database to retrieve, add, change, or remove information.
Query parameters concept
Extra name-and-value data added to a web address to tell a server how to handle a request.
R2 product
Cloudflare R2 is an object-storage service for storing files and other large data.
Raio product
Raio is Cloudflare's family of static certificate-transparency logs.
ransom demand concept
A ransom demand is a message from criminals asking for payment, usually to unlock systems or stop leaked data from being published.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
Raptor Cove product
An Intel CPU core architecture used in some modern processors.
RAT malware
A RAT, or remote access trojan, is malware that lets an attacker remotely control an infected device.
rate-limiting concept
Rate-limiting restricts how many requests someone can make in a set time to prevent abuse or overload.
RBAC concept
RBAC, or role-based access control, gives permissions based on a user’s assigned role.
RBAC permissions concept
RBAC permissions are role-based access control permissions that assign allowed actions based on a person’s role.
Read-Only concept
A permission setting that allows someone to view information but not change it.
Read-only Administrator concept
An administrative role that can view system settings and information without normally being able to change them.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
Real-Time Monitoring technique
Watching systems and activity as events happen so suspicious behavior can be found quickly.
real-time visibility concept
Real-time visibility means being able to see what is happening in systems or networks as it happens, rather than after the fact.
reassembly technique
Reassembly is the process of combining separate pieces of data or network packets into their original complete form.
Reboot concept
A reboot means restarting a computer, phone, server, or other device.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
recorded actions concept
Recorded actions are individual steps that a system logs as it performs tasks.
Recover concept
Recover is a cybersecurity function focused on restoring systems, data, and services after an incident.
Recovery key concept
A recovery key is a backup code or secret used to regain access to an account, device, or encrypted data.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
Registry Run keys technique
Registry Run keys are Windows settings that can automatically start programs when a user logs in, which attackers often abuse for persistence.
Regulations concept
Regulations are official rules that organizations must follow, often set by governments or industry authorities.
regulator concept
A regulator is an organization that oversees and enforces rules in a specific area.
regulatory compliance concept
Regulatory compliance means following laws and rules that apply to an organization or industry.
Reinforcement Learning technique
A machine-learning method in which a system learns by receiving rewards or penalties for its actions.
also: RL
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
relays concept
Relays are systems that pass network traffic or messages from one place to another, such as email servers forwarding mail between senders and recipients.
Release Cooldown technique
A safety delay before a newly published software package version is allowed to be installed.
also: one-day minimum release age, 24-hour release cooldown, release delay, age rule
release requests concept
Release requests are formal requests to approve or publish software, data, or changes.
remediate concept
To remediate means to fix a security problem or reduce the risk it creates.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
Remote Desktop concept
A technology that lets you see and control a computer's desktop from another device over a network.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
renewal automation technique
Renewal automation is the use of software to replace expiring certificates or credentials without manual work.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
repository scans technique
Repository scans are automated checks of source-code repositories to find secrets, vulnerabilities, malware, or policy violations.
Reproducible builds technique
A software-building method in which the same source code and settings produce identical program files every time.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
research environment concept
A research environment is a controlled setup used to study, test, or analyze software, systems, or attacks safely.
also: research environments
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
resolver protocol
A resolver is a DNS component that looks up domain names and returns the matching internet addresses or records.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Responder tool

Responsible AI concept
Responsible AI means designing and using artificial intelligence in ways that are safe, fair, accountable, and lawful.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
restitution concept
Restitution is money a court orders a defendant to pay back to victims for losses caused by a crime.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
Reuters organization
Reuters is an international news organization that reports on business, politics, technology, and security events.
reverse DNS protocol
Reverse DNS is the process of looking up the domain name associated with an IP address.
Reverse-engineer technique
To reverse-engineer something is to analyze how it works, often without having its original source code or design documents.
Reversibility concept
Reversibility is the degree to which an automated action can be undone if it causes harm.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
also: revoked, revocation events, revocation latency
RFC 10024 protocol
RFC 10024 is a technical Internet standard for the X25519MLKEM768 key-exchange method in TLS 1.3.
RFC 9773 other
RFC 9773 is an Internet standard that defines ACME Renewal Information for certificate replacement scheduling.
RFC 9964 protocol
An RFC is a technical specification published by the Internet Engineering Task Force, and this one defines a security-related standard.
RFC7523OAuthClientProvider tool
A software component referenced in security reporting that provides OAuth client authentication using an RFC 7523-style method.
Risk score concept
A risk score is a number or rating used to estimate how dangerous, suspicious, or vulnerable something is.
Role-Based Access technique
A method of granting permissions according to a person's job role rather than assigning each permission individually.
romance baiting technique
Romance baiting is a scam where criminals build a fake romantic relationship to gain trust and then push the victim into sending money or investing.
root concept
The superuser account on Unix and Linux systems that has unlimited control over the entire computer.
also: roots, brand-new root, existing root, established root
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
root password concept
A root password is the password for a highly privileged database or system account.
Root Password Hash concept
A protected mathematical representation of the root administrator's password on a Linux system.
root program concept
A root program is a browser or operating-system program that decides which certificate authorities are trusted.
also: root programs, root key programs, web root key programs
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
root-level access concept
Root-level access is the highest level of control on many systems, allowing someone to change almost anything.
Roskomnadzor organization
The Russian federal agency responsible for overseeing media, internet, and telecommunications censorship and regulation.
Rotterdam District Court organization
A court in Rotterdam, Netherlands, that handles legal cases in its district.
RSS 1.0/RDF protocol
RSS 1.0/RDF is an older web-feed format used to publish website updates for automated readers.
RSS 2.0 protocol
RSS 2.0 is a common web-feed format used by websites to publish updates that other software can collect.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service organization
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service is Russia's civilian foreign intelligence agency, also known as the SVR.
Russia-linked threat-actor
A description for threat actors or activity reported as having connections to Russia.
S3 product
S3 is Amazon’s cloud object-storage service, often used to store files, backups, logs, and website data.
S3 bucket product
An S3 bucket is an Amazon Web Services storage container used to hold files in the cloud.
s=google protocol
A DKIM selector value that tells email receivers which published Google signing key to use when checking a message signature.
SaaS platforms product
SaaS platforms are online software services that users access through the internet rather than installing locally.
SaaS services concept
SaaS services are software applications delivered over the internet rather than installed and managed locally.
SafeDep organization
SafeDep appears to be a security company or product focused on software supply chain risks.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
SAFER product
SAFER is a U.S. motor-carrier information system run by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
safety classifiers tool
Safety classifiers are automated systems that label content or behavior as safe, risky, or policy-violating.
Safety Systems concept
Automated rules, checks, and controls intended to reduce harmful or inappropriate use of a service.
salesforce product
Salesforce is a cloud platform for customer relationship management, sales, service, and business applications.
SAML protocol
SAML is a standard that lets users sign in once and access multiple services by passing trusted identity messages between them.
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
Sandbox Check technique
A security check that verifies whether code is staying within the limits of an isolated sandbox.
sandboxes tool
Sandboxes are isolated environments used to safely run and observe suspicious files or programs without risking a real system.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
Scam Center Strike Force organization
Scam Center Strike Force is an organization or law-enforcement initiative referenced in reporting about combating scam operations.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
Scanners tool
Scanners are tools that check systems, networks, or websites for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
scheduled task technique
A scheduled task is a job set to run automatically at a certain time or under certain conditions.
scheduled-tasks
Scheduled tasks are automated jobs on a computer that attackers can abuse to run malware at specific times or after reboot.
Scheduling concept
Scheduling is the process of planning when tasks, jobs, updates, or operations should run.
schema concept
A schema is a defined structure that describes how data should be organized and what fields it should contain.
Schema Learning technique
Schema Learning is a feature that observes normal request data and builds an expected structure for later security checks.
Schema Validation technique
Schema Validation is a security feature that checks whether incoming data follows an expected structure and format.
SCL=-1 concept
SCL=-1 is a Microsoft email spam score value that usually means a message is treated as trusted and bypasses normal spam filtering.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
scratch buffer concept
A scratch buffer is a temporary area of computer memory used while a program processes data.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.
Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna organization
An Italian university and research institution.
SDK concept
A collection of tools, libraries, and documentation that developers use to build applications for a specific platform.
Search engines concept
Search engines are services like Google or Bing that find and list web pages and other online content.
SEC organization
The SEC, or U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, is the U.S. regulator for securities markets and public company disclosures.
Security Analytics concept
Security Analytics is the practice or product category of analyzing security data to find threats, patterns, and risks.
Security and Quality Updates concept
Software updates that fix security problems, correct bugs, and improve reliability.
security architecture concept
Security architecture is the overall design of a system's protections, including how controls work together to reduce risk.
security controls concept
Security controls are safeguards, such as settings, tools, or policies, used to reduce risk.
security flaw vulnerability
A security flaw is a weakness in software, hardware, or a process that attackers could use to cause harm.
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
Security incidents concept
Security incidents are events that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems or data.
security operations concept
The function within an organization that continuously monitors, manages, and responds to cybersecurity threats.
Security operations center organization
A security operations center is a team or facility that monitors systems for cyber threats and coordinates response to incidents.
also: the DGFIP's SOC
security patch concept
A security patch is a software update that fixes a vulnerability or weakness attackers could exploit.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
Security reviews technique
Formal checks of a system or service to identify security risks before or after deployment.
also: accurate security reviews
security risks concept
Security risks are possible ways that systems, data, or people could be harmed by accidents, weaknesses, or attacks.
Security rules concept
Security rules are instructions that tell a system what activity to allow, block, alert on, or investigate.
security stack concept
A security stack is the collection of security tools and services an organization uses to protect its systems.
also: existing security tools
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security tools tool
Security tools are software or hardware products used to detect, prevent, investigate, or respond to cyber threats.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
self-hosted concept
Self-hosted means an organization runs software on servers it controls instead of using a vendor's cloud service.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive documents concept
Sensitive documents are files that contain private, confidential, legal, financial, or security-related information.
sensitive files concept
Sensitive files are files that contain private, secret, or valuable information that should not be exposed to unauthorized people.
sensitive financial data concept
Sensitive financial data is private money-related information, such as account numbers, payroll records, transactions, or banking details, that could cause harm if exposed.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
sensors tool
Devices or software components that collect data or monitor activity for analysis.
service account concept
A non-human account used by an application or service to perform automated tasks, often holding elevated privileges.
also: system principal
service account token theft technique
Service account token theft is when an attacker steals machine-account credentials to access cloud or internal systems as that account.
service account tokens concept
Service account tokens are digital credentials that let software or automated accounts access systems without a human logging in.
service accounts concept
Service accounts are accounts used by software or systems rather than by individual people.
service control policies concept
Service control policies are AWS Organizations rules that set maximum allowed permissions across AWS accounts.
Service discovery technique
A technique in which an attacker looks for network services, such as web servers, databases, or remote-access systems, that may be useful to target.
Service disruption concept
A service disruption is a period when an online service is unavailable, slow, or not working correctly for users.
Service Principal concept
A Microsoft Entra identity representing an application or service so it can receive permissions and sign in programmatically.
service providers organization
Service providers are companies or organizations that deliver services such as internet access, hosting, software platforms, or managed IT support.
service-account token protocol
A service-account token is a digital credential that lets an application or workload prove its identity to a system such as Kubernetes.
Services Australia organization
An Australian government agency that delivers public services and administers programs such as Medicare.
Servicing Branch concept
A shared code and update foundation used to maintain related versions of an operating system.
Session cookies concept
Session cookies are small browser-stored values that help websites remember a logged-in user during a visit.
session hijacking technique
Session hijacking is when an attacker steals or takes over a user’s logged-in web session so they can act as that user.
session IDs concept
Session IDs are unique temporary codes that tell a website or service which signed-in user session belongs to someone.
session revocation technique
Session revocation means ending a user’s active login sessions so stolen or old access can no longer be used.
session_id concept
A value used by a website to recognize and keep track of a user's active session.
setuid technique
setuid is a Unix permission setting that lets a program run with the privileges of the file’s owner, often root.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
SHA-256 concept
SHA-256 is a hashing method that creates a fixed-size digital fingerprint of data.
also: SHA-256 checksum
Shadowserver organization
Shadowserver is an internet security watchdog group that tracks exposed systems and other security data.
shared drive concept
A shared drive is a storage location where multiple users can access and collaborate on files.
shell tool
A shell is a command-line interface that lets a user or program run commands on a computer.
shell commands concept
Shell commands are text instructions typed into a command line to tell a computer what to do.
shellcode technique
Shellcode is small code used in exploits to make a vulnerable program run attacker-controlled commands.
shinyhunters
ShinyHunters is a cybercrime group known for stealing and selling large databases of user information.
ShinyHunters threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft, extortion, and selling stolen information.
SIEM product
A security tool that gathers and analyzes logs from across an organization in real time to spot suspicious activity.
also: a system that collects security logs
Signal product
A privacy-focused messaging app that encrypts calls and messages end-to-end, meaning only the sender and receiver can read them.
Signal Backup Recovery Keys concept
Signal Backup Recovery Keys are special keys used to restore encrypted Signal backups if a user needs to recover their messages.
Signal Secure Backups product
Signal Secure Backups is Signal's encrypted backup system for saving and restoring message history while protecting it from outsiders.
Simulations concept
Simulations are practice scenarios that imitate real events so people or systems can test how they would respond.
Single Sign On concept
Single Sign On lets a person log in once and then access multiple approved apps without signing in again each time.
Site isolation technique
Site isolation is a browser security feature that separates websites into different processes to reduce cross-site attacks.
slack
Slack is a workplace messaging and collaboration platform.
Snowflake product
Snowflake is a cloud data platform used to store and analyze data.
SOC organization
SOC stands for security operations center, a team or function that monitors and responds to security issues.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
also: bespoke social engineering
social media concept
Social media means online platforms where people share messages, photos, videos, and other content.
software concept
Software is the programs and apps that tell computers and devices what to do.
software supply chain security concept
Software supply chain security is the practice of protecting the code, tools, dependencies, and build systems used to create software.
source code concept
The human-readable code written by programmers that makes up software.
source control concept
Source control is a system for tracking changes to code so developers can collaborate and restore earlier versions.
source IP concept
A source IP is the internet address a network request appears to come from.
source IP address concept
A source IP address is the network address a connection or message comes from.
source IP addresses concept
Source IP addresses identify where network traffic appears to come from.
SpamExperts product
SpamExperts is an email-security service that filters spam and other unwanted or malicious messages.
spear-phishing technique
Spear-phishing is a targeted scam message crafted for a specific person or organization to trick them into revealing information or taking an unsafe action.
also: targeted phishing
spearphishing technique
Spearphishing is a targeted scam message sent to a specific person or group to trick them into giving access or information.
spearphishing-link
A spearphishing link is a targeted phishing message that includes a malicious link tailored to a specific person or organization.
Spectre v2 vulnerability
Spectre v2 is a class of processor vulnerability that can trick CPUs into leaking sensitive information through speculative execution behavior.
Speculative Execution concept
A processor performance feature that starts work based on a prediction before it knows whether that prediction is correct.
SPF protocol
SPF is an email check that verifies whether a sending server is allowed to send email for a domain.
SpiderMonkey product
Mozilla's JavaScript engine, used in Firefox and other software.
spies threat-actor
Spies are people who secretly collect information for another person, organization, or country.
splunk
Splunk is a platform for collecting and analyzing logs and security data.
spoof technique
To spoof something means to fake an identity, address, website, or message so it looks like it came from a trusted source.
spoofed technique
Spoofed means faked to look like it came from a trusted person, system, or address.
Spoofing technique
Spoofing is pretending to be someone or something trusted, such as an email sender, website, or device.
spyware malware
Spyware is malicious or intrusive software that secretly monitors a person’s device, messages, location, or activity.
SQL injection technique
SQL injection is a web attack where malicious database commands are inserted into an application's input fields or requests.
SQL Query technique
A command written in Structured Query Language that asks a database to find, organize, or change information.
SSH protocol
SSH is a secure way to remotely log in to and control another computer over a network.
SSH key concept
A cryptographic key used for password-less authentication to remote servers, a critical secret that attackers often steal for persistence.
SSH keys protocol
SSH keys are cryptographic login credentials used to securely access remote computers and services.
Stale concept
Stale means something is old or not recently used and may need review, updating, or removal.
standards-based proposal concept
A standards-based proposal is a suggested technical design intended to be reviewed and adopted through an industry standards process.
Star Blizzard threat-actor
Star Blizzard is a Russian-linked threat-actor group known for targeted phishing and cyber-espionage activity.
Startup concept
Startup usually refers to programs or scripts configured to run automatically when a computer or user session starts.
state-linked concept
State-linked describes activity believed to be connected to or supported by a national government.
stdio protocol
stdio is a standard way for a program to receive input and send output through local command-line streams.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen credential concept
A stolen credential is a password, token, or other login secret that an attacker has obtained.
stolen credentials concept
Stolen credentials are usernames, passwords, or login tokens that attackers have obtained without permission.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
Stolen passwords concept
Stolen passwords are passwords obtained by an attacker and used to access someone else’s account.
also: stolen staff logins, compromised accounts
su tool
su is a Unix/Linux command used to switch to another user account, often the root administrator account.
Subscribers protocol
In MQTT, devices or programs that receive messages from topics they have chosen to follow.
supervised release concept
Supervised release is a court-ordered period after prison when a person must follow legal conditions while monitored.
supply chain concept
A supply chain is the network of vendors, software, services, and processes an organization depends on to operate.
supply chain risk concept
Supply chain risk is the danger that software, services, or vendors you rely on could introduce security problems into your own systems.
Supply chain security concept
Supply chain security is the practice of protecting the outside software, vendors, services, and components an organization depends on.
supply-chain-attacks technique
Supply-chain-attacks are attacks that target the software or service creation process so many downstream users can be affected.
surveillance concept
The act of monitoring people or activities, often covertly, as part of espionage, law enforcement, or malware functions like keyloggers.
suspicious activity concept
Suspicious activity is behavior that looks unusual or risky and may indicate fraud, hacking, or policy violations.
Suspicious files concept
Suspicious files are files that look unusual or potentially harmful and may need investigation.
systems concept
Systems are organized sets of hardware, software, or processes working together.
tactics concept
In cybersecurity, tactics are the broad goals behind an attacker's actions, such as gaining access, stealing data, or staying hidden.
taiwan other
Taiwan is a territory in East Asia that is often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regional targeting or geopolitical activity.
Take Control product
Take Control is a remote access and support product used by IT teams to connect to customer devices.
Talos organization
Talos, also known as Cisco Talos, is Cisco's threat intelligence and security research organization.
Talos IR organization
Talos IR is Cisco Talos's incident response team that helps organizations investigate and recover from cyberattacks.
Targeted attacks concept
Targeted attacks are cyberattacks aimed at specific people, organizations, or systems rather than random victims.
Technical analysis concept
Technical analysis is a detailed examination of how a system, vulnerability, malware sample, or attack works.
Technical findings concept
Technical findings are the concrete details a researcher discovers, such as what was vulnerable, exposed, or misconfigured.
Technical information concept
Technical information is detailed data about systems, software, configurations, or operations.
Technical recommendations concept
Technical recommendations are practical security steps or configuration advice meant to reduce risk or fix problems.
Technical Vulnerability vulnerability
A weakness in software, hardware, or configuration that an attacker could use to compromise a system.
Technology Stacks concept
The collection of software, services, devices, and platforms an organization uses to run its technology.
Telemetry concept
Telemetry is data automatically collected from systems or devices to show what they are doing and whether something looks wrong.
also: events and telemetry
tenant concept
A tenant is a separate customer space inside a shared cloud or software service.
tenfold product
tenfold is a software product for managing access, permissions, and reviews of shared business content.
tenfold Software organization
tenfold Software is the company that provides the tenfold access-governance product.
terabytes concept
A terabyte is a large unit of digital storage, roughly equal to one trillion bytes.
test environment concept
A test environment is a separate place for trying changes safely before using them in real live systems.
test environments concept
Test environments are separate systems used to safely try software or security changes before using them on real live systems.
Test Tenant concept
A separate cloud environment used to test applications, settings, or accounts before using them in a production environment.
Tez Tour organization
Tez Tour is a Russian travel and tour-operator company.
The Australian organization
The Australian is a national newspaper and media organization in Australia.
The Information organization
The Information is a technology-focused news publication that reports on companies, startups, and the tech industry.
The Record organization
A cybersecurity news publication.
The Wall Street Journal organization
The Wall Street Journal is a major U.S. newspaper that reports on business, finance, politics, and technology.
also: The Journal
Third parties concept
Third parties are outside companies or services that are separate from the main organization and the user.
third-party concept
A third party is an outside person, company, or service that is involved but is not the main organization or customer.
third-party services concept
Third-party services are outside companies or platforms an organization uses to help run its business or technology.
third-party vendors organization
Third-party vendors are outside companies that provide products or services to an organization.
threat actor threat-actor
A threat actor is the person, group, or organization carrying out a cyberattack.
Threat actors concept
Threat actors are people or groups that carry out harmful activity against computers, websites, or organizations.
Threat detection concept
The process of identifying malicious or suspicious activities on a network or system before they cause damage.
Threat Event concept
A Threat Event is a record that links a security indicator to its source report, tags, and related context.
Threat Events Platform product
Threat Events Platform is a service for investigating security events, indicators, tags, and related threat-intelligence information.
threat hunting technique
Threat hunting is the proactive search for signs that attackers may already be inside a network or system.
Threat hunts technique
Threat hunts are proactive searches through systems and data to find attackers who may have slipped past automatic defenses.
threat intelligence concept
Threat intelligence is information collected and analyzed about possible or active cyber threats.
Threat Intelligence dataset concept
A threat intelligence dataset is a collection of security information about possible threats, such as suspicious addresses, files, or attacker activity.
threat intelligence feed concept
A threat intelligence feed is a stream of data about known threats, such as malicious IP addresses, domains, or malware indicators.

Threat Signals is a Cloudflare service that turns selected reporting from RSS feeds into private threat-intelligence data.
threat window concept
The period of time between when a vulnerability is discovered and when it is patched, during which systems are exposed.
threats concept
Threats are possible dangers that could harm systems, data, devices, or users.
Timeline tool
A security investigation view that arranges events in time order to help analysts understand what happened.
TLS protocol
TLS is the security protocol that encrypts many internet connections, including HTTPS websites.
TLS 1.3 protocol
TLS 1.3 is a modern version of the security protocol that encrypts many internet connections, including HTTPS websites.
TLS certificates protocol
TLS certificates are digital certificates that help websites prove their identity and encrypt connections, shown by HTTPS in a browser.
token concept
A digital piece of data used for authentication, authorization, or as a session identifier.
token endpoint protocol
A token endpoint is the server address in OAuth-like systems where an app exchanges credentials or codes for access tokens.
tokens concept
Digital objects used for authentication, identification, or authorization, like access tokens.
Traces concept
Detailed records that show the path and timing of work through an application or distributed system.
Transparency concept
Transparency means being open and clear about what is happening, such as how data is collected, used, or shared.
Trellix organization
A cybersecurity company (formerly McAfee Enterprise) that provides endpoint protection, threat detection, and other security products.
triage concept
The process of quickly sorting and prioritizing security alerts to decide which ones need immediate attention.
Triangle product
Triangle is a purported cryptocurrency investment platform referenced in security reporting.
trust store concept
A trust store is a list of trusted certificate authorities that a browser, operating system, or device uses to verify websites.
also: trust store coverage
Trusted concept
Trusted means treated as reliable or allowed by a system, person, or policy.
Trusted Execution Environment concept
A protected part of a device's processor designed to handle sensitive code and data separately from normal apps.
trusted services concept
Trusted services are online systems or services that users and organizations normally rely on and accept as legitimate.
tunneling technique
Tunneling is a way to carry one kind of network traffic inside another connection, often to hide it or pass through restrictions.
two-factor authentication concept
An extra login step beyond a password, such as a code sent to your phone, that greatly improves account security.
typescript tool
TypeScript is a programming language built on JavaScript that adds extra checks to help developers catch mistakes.
typosquat technique
A typosquat is a lookalike name meant to be confused with a legitimate name.
typosquatted technique
Typosquatted means using a lookalike name or domain that relies on users making typing mistakes.
typosquatting technique
Typosquatting is when attackers use names that look like legitimate websites or packages to trick people who make small typing mistakes.
U.S. Air Force organization
The branch of the United States military responsible for air and space operations.
U.S. authorities organization
Federal government agencies in the United States, such as the FBI or CISA, responsible for enforcing laws and cybersecurity.
U.S. citizens concept
U.S. citizens are people who legally hold citizenship of the United States.
U.S. Department of Justice organization
The U.S. Department of Justice is the U.S. government department responsible for federal law enforcement and legal prosecutions.
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission organization
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is the federal agency that regulates securities markets and requires certain public company disclosures.
Uber organization
Uber is a ride-hailing and delivery company whose services and data can appear in privacy or security stories.
UDP protocol
UDP is a core internet protocol that sends data quickly without setting up a reliable connection first.
ukraine other
Ukraine is a country in Eastern Europe that is often discussed in cybersecurity because of major cyberattacks linked to regional conflict.
Umbreon other
A fictional Pokémon character often depicted as a black, cat-like creature with yellow markings.
Unauthorized Actions concept
Actions taken without the required permission or approval.
unauthorized activity concept
Unauthorized activity is access or behavior in a system that was not allowed by the owner.
Unit 42 organization
The threat intelligence and research team at Palo Alto Networks that publishes reports on cyber threats and vulnerabilities.
united-kingdom
The United Kingdom is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
united-states
The United States is a country often referenced in cybersecurity stories as a target, source, regulator, or law-enforcement actor.
Universal SSL product
Universal SSL is Cloudflare's service that provides TLS certificates for websites using its network.
UnJS organization
An organization and open-source project ecosystem that develops JavaScript and TypeScript tools.
unlock() technique
unlock() is a function-style name often used in smart contracts or programs to release a lock or allow an operation to proceed.
unsafe concept
Unsafe means code or behavior that can bypass normal safety checks and may cause crashes, bugs, or security risks if used incorrectly.
Unused concept
Unused means something exists but does not appear to be currently used by the system or workflow being reviewed.
Unusual activity concept
Unusual activity is behavior on an account, device, or network that looks different from normal and may signal a problem.
upm tool
A lightweight TypeScript package manager for installing and managing packages from the npm registry.
upm.lock product
A lockfile used by upm to record the exact versions of software packages in a project.
upstream concept
Upstream refers to the original source or earlier supplier of software, code, data, or services that others depend on.

UPX is a program packer that compresses executable files and is sometimes used by malware authors to make analysis harder.
Urgent concept
Urgent is a priority label meaning something needs quick attention or action.
URL shortener tool
A URL shortener is a service that turns a long web address into a shorter link, which can also hide where the link really goes.
URL-encoding technique
URL-encoding is a way to represent special characters in a web address using percent signs and character codes.
user agents concept
User agents are identifiers that browsers, apps, or bots send to websites to describe the software making the request.
user behavior concept
User behavior is how people act when using systems, such as clicking links, reporting emails, or logging in.
user credentials concept
User credentials are login details, such as usernames, passwords, tokens, or keys, used to prove someone's identity.
user data concept
User data is information about people or accounts, such as names, settings, files, or activity history.
User Group concept
A collection of user accounts that can receive the same access policy together.
User-Agent protocol
A User-Agent is a browser or app identifier sent to websites so the site knows what kind of client is connecting.
UUID concept
A UUID is a long unique identifier used by software to label something without confusing it with something else.
also: universally unique identifier
Valid account abuse technique
A technique in which an attacker uses real accounts or stolen legitimate credentials to access systems while appearing authorized.
validation concept
Validation is the process of checking that data, settings, or actions meet expected rules before accepting them.
Verified concept
Verified is a status label that usually means an account, seller, or item has been checked or approved by a platform.
version control concept
A system for tracking changes to files, especially software code, so earlier versions can be reviewed or restored.
victim concept
A victim is the person or organization harmed or targeted by an attack, scam, or crime.
victims concept
Victims are people or organizations harmed or targeted by a cyberattack or scam.
Victorian Department of Health organization
A government department responsible for public health services in the Australian state of Victoria.
vietnam other
Vietnam is a country in Southeast Asia.
Viewer product
Viewer is a product role or component that displays information or lets someone observe a session or system.
virtual machine concept
A virtual machine is a software-based computer that runs inside another computer like a separate device.
visibility concept
Visibility means being able to see and understand activity across users, devices, applications, and data.
Visibility gap concept
A visibility gap is an area of a system, network, or process that defenders cannot clearly monitor or understand.
VPN concept
A VPN is a tool that creates a private connection to a network over the internet.
VPN credentials concept
VPN credentials are the usernames, passwords, or keys used to connect to a private network remotely.
